description: This composite figure group combines one data table with two mechanical-property plots for an Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel plate processed by intercritical quenching-annealing. The table (austenite volume fraction, %) lists, by EBSD, HR ~16, IQ-1050 ~7, QA-620 ~28, QA-680 ~35, QA-740 ~50, QA-800 ~49; by XRD the entries are "/" for HR and IQ-1050 (not measured) and ~33, ~37, ~51, ~48 for QA-620 through QA-800. Panel (a) plots engineering stress (MPa, 0–1200) versus engineering strain (%, 0–70) with six labelled curves: HR, IQ-1050, QA-620 (blue), QA-680 (green), QA-740 (purple), QA-800 (gold). HR reaches the highest stress (~1100 MPa) at only ~4–5% strain; IQ-1050 peaks near 900 MPa at ~2%; the QA curves show lower plateaus (~700–850 MPa) but far larger elongation, QA-740 extending to near 70%. Panel (b) plots work hardening rate (MPa, 0–8000) against true strain ε (0–0.5) for QA-620/680/740/800 only, annotated "ε = 0.01". All WHR curves collapse from ~8000 MPa at ε≈0 to ~1000–1300 MPa by ε≈0.1 then plateau; QA-620 stays highest between ε 0.01–0.1, and curves diverge beyond ε≈0.15, reflecting different TRIP activity.

subfigures.description: Two-row data table of austenite volume fraction (%) for six conditions (HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740, QA-800), row 1 'By EBSD': ~16, ~7, ~28, ~35, ~50, ~49; row 2 'By XRD': '/', '/', ~33, ~37, ~51, ~48. Header row holds the sample labels.

Engineering stress (MPa, 0–1200) versus engineering strain (%, 0–70). Six curves labelled HR (black), IQ-1050 (red), QA-620 (blue), QA-680 (green), QA-740 (purple), QA-800 (gold). HR reaches the highest peak (~1100 MPa) at short strain; IQ-1050 peaks ~900 MPa at ~2%; QA curves plateau ~700–850 MPa with much larger elongations, QA-740 reaching ~70%.

Work hardening rate (MPa, 0–8000) versus true strain ε (0–0.5) for QA-620 (blue), QA-680 (green), QA-740 (purple), QA-800 (gold), with an arrow annotation 'ε = 0.01'. All curves fall steeply from ~8000 MPa to ~1000–1300 MPa by ε≈0.1 then plateau; QA-620 is highest over ε 0.01–0.1; curves diverge after ε≈0.15; QA-680 drops first, QA-740 extends to ~0.53.

observations.observation: The table reports austenite volume fraction (%) measured by EBSD as ~16 (HR), ~7 (IQ-1050), ~28 (QA-620), ~35 (QA-680), ~50 (QA-740) and ~49 (QA-800).
The table reports austenite volume fraction (%) measured by XRD as ~33 (QA-620), ~37 (QA-680), ~51 (QA-740) and ~48 (QA-800), while the HR and IQ-1050 cells contain '/' (not measured).
Panel (a) axes are labelled Engineering Stress/Mpa (0–1200) versus Engineering Strain/% (0–70), with a legend listing HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800.
In panel (a) HR (black) reaches the highest stress, peaking near the 1100 MPa gridline at only ~4–5% strain, and IQ-1050 (red) peaks near 900 MPa at ~2% strain.

In panel (a) the QA curves plateau at lower stress (~700–850 MPa) but attain much larger elongations, with QA-740 (purple) extending to nearly 70% strain and QA-680 (green) and QA-800 (gold) ending near 45–48%.
Panel (b) axes are labelled Work hardening rate/Mpa (0–8000) versus True strain/ε (0–0.5) and shows only QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800, with a pointing annotation 'ε = 0.01'.
In panel (b) all WHR curves collapse steeply from ~8000 MPa at ε≈0 to ~1000–1300 MPa by ε≈0.1, then remain near-plateau; QA-620 stays highest for ε 0.01–0.1, and the curves diverge beyond ε≈0.15.
The caption states panel (a) shows engineering stress-strain curves of HR, IQ-1050 and QA specimens and panel (b) shows work hardening rate curves of QA specimens.
The caption states the figure/table reports the austenite volume fraction (%) of the experimental steel measured by EBSD and XRD.
The citing text states the hot-rolled steel (HR) had the highest tensile strength of ~1107 MPa with poor total elongation of ~5.6%.

The citing text states that after intercritical quenching (IQ-1050) the yield strength improved to ~575 MPa versus HR, while tensile strength fell to ~929 MPa and total elongation was ~2.0%, the poorest of all specimens.

The citing text attributes the higher WHR of QA-620 over true strain 0.01–0.1 to precipitated carbides intensely retarding dislocation gliding, and the divergence of QA curves after true strain 0.15 to different levels of TRIP effect.
